newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS-up slightly, focus on primary.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS-up slightly, focus on primary.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices were up a touch in light activity as the primary market took center stage on Tuesday.
About $1 billion is slated for sale, including a New York City $200 million general obligation bond offering.
"It is pretty quiet, the focus is on primary," a trader said. "We are probably up a touch." "The levels are very high and guys are looking at new issues."
Monday's quiet session ended modestly higher, market participants said.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was unchanged at 96-17/32 to yield 6.90 percent in New York trade.
Turning to new issues, Tuesday's municipal bond sales are expected to total $1 billion in 41 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings are expected total $559 million in 20 sales, with a $92.2 million New York State Dormitory Authority deal through Merrill Lynch & Co. topping the list.

A $32 million Health and Educational Facilties Board of the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County, Tenn., revenue refunding bond issue, 1997 Series A, for The Vanderbilt University, was priced with a top yield of 5.60 in 2018 by Goldman Sachs & Co.
The retail scale on a $93 million Dauphin County General Authority Health System revenue bonds, Series of 1997, for Pinnacle Health System project, Pa., was released by Smith Barney Inc.
On the competitive side, 21 sales totaling $470 million are scheduled. A $200 million New York City deal is the largest at 1000 EDT.
An additional 10 sales totaling $402 million are on the possible calendar, meaning underwriters have said they may price the issues Tuesday depending on market conditions.
